name: fanin64_2d_add
targeted_gap: High fan-in inflates bytes_per_elem so budget_target and the inner_floor both collapse BELOW the default 32, and the 2-D distributor pins the outer dim at 1 -> a [1,16] tile vs the default's [32,32].
hypothesis: 64 full-extent fp32 loads + 1 store => bytes_per_elem=260, budget_target=8192//260=31, so inner_floor=min(256,pow2_floor(31)=16)=16 and the seed emits [1,16] (16 elems/program). The default [32,32] moves a 1024-element 2-D tile (64x larger, coalesced across 32 rows). The starved [1,16] tile launches 64x more programs with tiny per-program work and poor L2 reuse of the 64 operands, so it should run >10% slower than default.

name: fanin32_2d_silu
targeted_gap: Even at 32 fp32 inputs (a realistic multi-residual/expert combine) plus per-element SiLU compute, the byte budget clamps the seed to [1,32] while the register cap (reg_cap=496) never binds, so the tile is starved on the WIDTH axis, not the register axis the fix was meant to protect.
hypothesis: 32 fp32 loads + store => bytes_per_elem=132, budget_target=8192//132=62 -> pow2 32, inner_floor=32, seed=[1,32] (32 elems). Default=[32,32]=1024 elems (32x larger). The reg_cap is 496 (not binding), so the register-cap fix does nothing here; the seed is starved purely by the bandwidth budget. A 32x-smaller 2-D tile with heavier per-element math should lose >10% to the default.

name: fanin96_bf16_2d
targeted_gap: The gap is not fp32-specific: with bf16 STORAGE (2B) it takes more inputs, but 96 bf16 operands still push bytes_per_elem to 194 -> budget 42 -> clamped to [1,32], while reg_bytes_per_elem=388 (fp32 compute) makes reg_cap=168 -- so BOTH caps agree on a sub-default tile.
hypothesis: 96 bf16 loads + 1 bf16 store => bytes_per_elem=(97)*2=194, budget_target=8192//194=42 -> pow2 32; reg_bytes_per_elem=97*4=388, reg_cap=65536//388=168. min -> 42, inner_floor=32, seed=[1,32] (32 elems). Default [32,32]=1024 (32x larger). A huge-traffic bf16 combine gets a starved [1,32] tile that under-fills each program and re-reads all 96 operand streams with poor coalescing across only 32 contiguous elements, so >10% slower than default.
